title: Jude and the Bridge
premise: In the river town of Marrow's Bend, Silas Ashgrove has survived her indenture to the Halloway Trading Company by being useful and unremarkable. When the army requisitions the town, its warehouses, and the company ledger bearing every diver's name, she learns that a boy she once promised to help cross the border bridge—Jude, son of a pearl diver branded an enemy of the crown—is now hunted. Silas must choose between the loyalty of her found family among the divers and the truth that will expose them all: forging the ledger to erase Jude's name means erasing her own history too. In the end, she burns the ledger at the bridge itself, freeing every name on it, and crosses over with Jude into an uncertain but unowned life.
about_author: Ansel Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing shipping ledgers from coastal trading towns before turning to fiction. They write about ordinary people whose names history nearly forgot.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Names
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In peacetime Marrow's Bend, Silas works the counting-house by day and the shallows by dusk, invisible among the pearl divers who have become her only family. She secretly promises young Jude—a diver's son facing conscription—that if war ever comes, she'll get him across the old bridge. Emotional beat: quiet tenderness masking fear of attachment.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The army arrives, seizes the trading company, and confiscates the master ledger containing every diver's name—including forged entries Silas made years ago to protect others. Her employer's son, now a collaborating officer, begins auditing the books. She realizes her forgeries could hang half the waterfront. Emotional beat: dread as invisibility collapses into exposure.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, with a tense interlude in the officer's perspective as he grows suspicious of her neat columns. Jude returns to town in secret; soldiers are closing on the bridge crossing. Silas must forge one final entry—erasing Jude while implicating herself—to buy him a night's head start. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. self-preservation reaching breaking point.

chapters.title: Jude and the Bridge
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At dawn, Silas carries the ledger to the bridge where soldiers await Jude. Instead of surrendering him, she sets the book alight—every name, debt, and indenture curling to ash—and walks beside Jude past the stunned guard, claiming the divers' freedom as her own confession. Emotional beat: cathartic sacrifice resolving into hard-won hope.
